title.zh: 实际坐标圆环磁通矩阵

summary: Build the dense actual-coordinate flux matrix for an R,Z node grid.

capability: Build the dense actual-coordinate flux matrix for an R,Z node grid.
operation: matching R,Z grids -> target-row/source-column psi response
discovery.model: Axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux with zero diagonal for active source nodes.
discovery.geometry: Finite rectilinear or irregular two-dimensional coordinate arrays.
discovery.boundary: Axis rows and zero-radius source columns are zero, and duplicate positive-radius nodes are rejected.

identity.direction: matching R,Z grids to target-row/source-column psi response
identity.definition: Flatten matching R,Z arrays in C order and evaluate every actual target/source pair.
identity.model: Axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux with zero diagonal for active source nodes.
identity.geometry: Finite rectilinear or irregular 2-D coordinate arrays.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; matrix entries Wb/rad/A.
identity.boundary: Axis rows and zero-radius source columns are zero; duplicate positive-radius nodes are rejected.
assumptions: Inputs are finite real matching 2-D arrays.
The matrix is dense and uses the explicit zero-self convention.

outputs.name: G
outputs.description: Flux response matrix with target rows/source columns

preconditions: Inputs are finite real matching 2-D arrays.
The matrix is dense and uses the explicit zero-self convention.
supported: Irregular/asymmetric coordinates, permutation covariance, axis limits, and duplicate/complex failures.
excluded: Finite-conductor self-inductance, extreme-scale qualification, and equilibrium claims.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for malformed, complex, nonfinite, negative-radius, or duplicate active nodes.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError from an unrepresentable kernel response propagates.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct matrix evaluation.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No matrix is returned after validation or kernel failure.

example.description: Build a dense matrix from a 3x3 irregular R,Z mesh.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.electromagnetism import get_gpsi
R,Z=np.meshgrid([.4,.8,1.2],[-.5,0.,.9])
G=get_gpsi(R,Z)
assert G.shape==(9,9) and np.all(np.diag(G)==0)
example.expected: The result is a finite (9,9) matrix with an exactly zero diagonal.

scope: Original irregular and unchanged uniform geometry
Independent asymmetric heldout integral and permutation oracle
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent numerical relation/invariants in named cases; no general extreme-scale or conductor model qualification.
known_limitations: Zero-self is a limited discrete model
No finite wire, singular pair or physical equilibrium solution claim
